plan.title: core-guard: content-aware package pin + lock follow-through (tighten #3127 path allowlist)

narratives.Description: The #3127 path-only allowlist lets package.json and lockfiles co-travel with .deft/core/** on upgrade PRs, but any edit to those paths is exempt. This story tightens the deposited deft-core-guard so package/lock co-travel is content-constrained to the @deftai/directive pin unit and necessary lock follow-through.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem
#3127 / PR #3138 correctly expanded `deft-core-guard` so a normal framework upgrade is **one PR**: deposit + `@deftai/directive` pin/lock + `.deft/GENERATION.json`.

The v1 implementation is **path-only** for `package.json` and lockfiles. That matches the #3127 note (“path-level allow is OK for v1; stricter pin-only is nicer if cheap”).

Residual risk: a PR that mixes `.deft/core/**` with **unrelated** package/lock edits (other deps, scripts, metadata) can still pass the guard because those paths are unconditionally exempted when present.

Consumer Greptile reviews on upgrade PRs now flag this as P2 (path-only) or, when operators hand-roll content checks in the consumer workflow, as a long P1 chase that does not belong in app repos.

## Goal
Tighten the **deposited** guard so package/lock co-travel is content-constrained:

| File | Pass only when |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | Diff is `@deftai/directive*` **dependency-key** pin change only (not scripts/settings that merely contain the substring) |
| lockfile(s) | Follow-through for that pin (identity + necessary transitive/resolution lines), **not** unrelated direct product dependency identity or metadata-only product edits riding the exemption |
| `.deft/GENERATION.json` | Remains path-allowlisted as upgrade stamp |

## Must still fail
- `.deft/core/**` + true app/product source
- `.deft/core/**` + package/lock changes that are not the Directive pin unit

## Non-goals
- Removing the mixed core+app guard
- Requiring two stacked upgrade PRs again
- Per-consumer hand-rolled guard forks (fix ships in the deposit)

## Acceptance
- [ ] Deposit + Directive pin + lock follow-through + GENERATION (+ installer-managed paths) **passes**
- [ ] Deposit + unrelated package.json field / unrelated lock identity or product metadata **fails**
- [ ] Documented in UPGRADING next to the one-upgrade-PR shape
- [ ] Classifier/guard tests cover pin-only vs mixed package cases (npm + at least one lock format used in CI)
- [ ] No consumer needs to patch `deft-core-guard.yml` to land a normal upgrade

## Context
- Parent: #3127 (path allowlist v1), #1430 (guard origin), #3117 (GENERATION)
- Observed: consumer upgrade reviews rate path-only as residual weakness; incomplete consumer-side content forks thrash review without fixing product SoT

## Refs
- #3127
- #1430
- #3117
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer landing a normal framework upgrade, I want deft-core-guard to accept deposit + Directive pin + lock follow-through while rejecting unrelated package or lock edits, so that residual path-only weakness does not force hand-rolled consumer guard forks.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Locate classifier for no-mixed-core-and-app / installerManagedMatchers in packages/core/src/init-deposit/hygiene.ts and the deposited workflow body from scaffold coreGuardWorkflowContent. 2. Add content-aware checks: package.json diff may only change @deftai/directive* dependency-key pins (not scripts/settings that merely contain the substring); lockfiles allow only follow-through for that pin (identity + necessary transitive lines), not unrelated direct product deps. 3. Keep .deft/GENERATION.json path-allowlisted. 4. Fail on .deft/core/** + true app source or package/lock not the pin unit. 5. Tests in hygiene.test.ts (and related) for pin-only vs mixed npm + at least one lock format used in CI. 6. Document in content/UPGRADING.md next to one-upgrade-PR shape; CHANGELOG #3193. Verify: npm test -w @deftai/directive-core -- --run init-deposit/hygiene.

narrative.Acceptance: Given deposit + @deftai/directive* dependency-key pin change only + GENERATION + installer-managed paths, when the guard classifies the PR, then it passes.
Given lockfile changes that only follow through the Directive pin identity and necessary transitive/resolution lines, when mixed with core deposit, then the guard passes.
Given .deft/core/** plus unrelated package.json field edits or unrelated lock product dependency identity, when the guard runs, then it fails.

Given UPGRADING one-upgrade-PR section and unit tests, when reviewed, then pin-only vs mixed cases are documented and covered for npm plus at least one CI lock format; no consumer must patch deft-core-guard.yml for a normal upgrade.
